issues.description: In the solution repository, PersonService.deletePerson accepts a Person object (public void deletePerson(Person person)), but the server-side API (and the problem statement) define the DELETE endpoint as DELETE /persons/{personId} which passes a UUID path variable. The solution's PersonResource.deletePerson method calls personService.deletePerson(personId) (passing a UUID). This creates a parameter-type mismatch between the controller and the service in the solution, and also conflicts with the template/service expectation (template PersonService.deletePerson(UUID)). Students following the problem statement and template would implement and call deletePerson(UUID), but the solution shows a different service signature. This inconsistency is structural and would cause compilation/runtime errors or confusion when comparing template, problem description, and the reference solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the service signature consistent with the API and template. Change PersonService.deletePerson in the solution to accept a UUID (public void deletePerson(UUID personId)) and remove the person by ID (e.g., persons.removeIf(p -> p.getId().equals(personId))). Alternatively, change PersonResource.deletePerson to resolve a Person instance and pass that to the service, but the simpler and clearer fix is to revert the service method to accept UUID so it aligns with DELETE /persons/{personId} and the template.
